query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of 1-2 vol% of TiC nanoparticles via powder metallurgy and hot isostatic pressing, with optimized parameters to ensure uniform distribution, will improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) with dual-phase lamellar colonies
generation.intervention: Introduction of 1-2 vol% of TiC nanoparticles via powder metallurgy and hot isostatic pressing
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoparticle-matrix interface and nanoparticle-induced grain refinement
generation.mechanism: The introduction of TiC nanoparticles refines the grain size of the lamellar colonies, increases the density of internal boundaries, and provides additional sites for dislocation nucleation and propagation, thereby enhancing strength and ductility. The nanoparticles can also act as crack arresters, reducing the propensity for microcracking and catastrophic damage.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength (up to 15%) and room-temperature tensile ductility (up to 20%) relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline
generation.boundary: The intervention is bounded by the material system (eutectic high-entropy alloy) and operating conditions (room-temperature tensile deformation)
generation.uncertainty: The uncertainty lies in the optimal content and distribution of TiC nanoparticles, as well as the potential risks of nanoparticle agglomeration or uneven distribution
